catalogue.m1l: pixels differing from the Figma render
catalogue.note: Read from the Figma file (page “old website”, frame “Desktop”), class for class from the design context. The content column inside the frame is scaled in the file by about 1.196 (the 140px logo reads 167.45), so values are fractional; they are built as read, not rounded. Figma lays lines and paragraph gaps on whole pixels (35px, not 34.54; 33, not 32.89) and so does this build. Two instance values came from the Plugin API, because the design context gave the main component’s: the nav “More” and “Log in” are 18.09px, not 29.75, and the phone’s “Back” label is centred in its button. The faint crowd behind the testimonials (283 vector pieces at 12% opacity, 1.9 MB as SVG) ships as one 2x image rendered from Figma’s own SVG exports; the phone screenshots are the file’s images at 2x, WebP. 357 image layers that sit wholly outside the frame (an off-canvas copy of the testimonials) are left out; they drew nothing. The phone status bar is SF Pro Text, which cannot be served: it shows in the system face. What remains in the diff is glyph and vector edges, 1px baselines on some sizes where Chrome and Figma round half-leading differently, and a 1.645px divider Chrome inks on one row where Figma spreads it over three.
